title: Forge operator ending args v1 (a payload value at event_schema 1)
description: The shape of operator/commanded.args for an operator's typed ending (decision 0064 rulings 4 and 5, choice 7), and for nothing else. This is not a widening of the v1 event envelope: 'command' is already an open string there and 'args' an already-legal open object the reducer never reads, so a new command word with structured args is a v1 event byte for byte — no new event type, no new payload field, no manifest digest moved. classify writes the annotation on a run that has already stopped; stop carries it in the command that ends its run. A completed run cannot be classified: its ending is 'shipped' or 'shipped-flagged' by ruling 6's ending-implies-status table, and no operator cause names either. Where fold admits an operator annotation it changes nothing (the 'OperatorCommanded | OperatorRejected' arm). No operator/accepted follows a classify: there is nothing to execute, and fold refuses an acceptance on a terminal run by design. The annotation is read by brokkr-view and the fleet dossier, never by fold, and RunState gains nothing from it.

cause.description: Exactly decision 0064 ruling 4's six operator-owned endings. The policy endings and 'unclassified' are derived, never named by an operator, and are refused here.

by.description: The run that replaced this one, and the realm it was read in. Required with 'superseded' and refused with every other cause.

realm.description: The realm whose journal the cited run was read in, keyed as decision 0026 ruling 3 keys every fleet fact. Null in a one-hearth world, which is every world that never drew a second journal.

run_id.description: The run that replaced this one. It must exist in the journal 'realm' names (the workspace journal when null), and need not be finished: a re-commission is usually fired in the same minute.

ref.description: The commit or pull request the work landed by, recorded as written and never resolved. Required with 'delivered-elsewhere' and refused with every other cause.

reason.description: The operator's own sentence. classify writes it here rather than on an operator/accepted, because a classify has no acceptance: the commanded event is the whole record. An accepted stop may carry its sentence on its acceptance, so this is not required by this schema.
